sources.note: Nothing on Alangan stress. Alangan appears in pronoun Table 4.42 (p.146) and a handful of etyma written with Tagalog-style accent diacritics (ALANGAN labû, sǝkdǝ̀, akpǝlǝs, patarata), implying Lobel heard both final- and penult-accented words; sec. 8.2.9 'Contrastive accent' is about Manide/Inagta Alabat; fn. 3 p.286 is a general remark that most Mindanao languages lost contrastive stress.

sources.note: Silent on Alangan/North Mangyan accent. Alangan (and Iraya, Tadyawan) forms are cited without accent marks while Hanunoo/Buhid forms carry accents; only accent remarks are fn. 9 (definition of aphesis) and a p.578 aside on Bisayan -an suffixes distinguished by accent.

sources.citation: Zorc, R. David. [1972]. Alangan (barrio Paitan, Naujan, Oriental Mindoro) field data: Proto-Austronesian worksheet (500 items), Proto-Philippine grammatical worksheet, handwritten notes and texts. 40 pp. page images. zorc.net/RDZorc/Alangan/ (= sealang.net/archives/zorc).
sources.note: No prose statement. Primary data with acute accent marked on most forms: majority penultimate (bayápun 'afternoon', búris 'ashes', bálay 'house', kapúniʔ 'yesterday', lakúnaw 'big') but many final (akó 'I', kamí 'we', duwáy 'two', isdáʔ 'fish', daʔətə́n 'bad/ugly', budáŋ 'child', atáy 'here', istá 'there'); i.e. the transcription implies accent position is not fixed, but Zorc states no rule.
